pr_title: Fix Life360 recovery from server errors

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
If communication with the Life360 is interrupted for any reason, the state of
all the entities become `unavailable`. However, after communication is restored,
the state of the entities does not return to normal right away like it should.
Eventually, when the server has new data for an entity it will update and return
to normal.

This change makes the entities return to normal as soon as communication with
the server is restored.

> Should this be tagged for 2022.8.1?

This is fixing a bug that doesn't have all that much impact. First, it only happens if there is a server communication failure (e.g., network outage.) Second, it's only making sure the entities return to their "normal" state immediately after communication is reestablished. Without this fix the entities will return to "normal" on their own the next time the server has new data for them. The lag is really only an inconvenience, but it does cause user confusion, which is why it needs to be fixed, and released to the field sooner rather than later.

As to whether it should be tagged, I'm not sure how those decisions are made.

> As to whether it should be tagged, I'm not sure how those decisions are made.

You get to make the suggestion. In this case, I would recommend it.

Thanks.

Yes, I did mean to change DataUpdateCoordinator to Life360DataUpdateCoordinator in this module, but I was focusing on the bug and trying to get a fix out. In fact, I'm working on a significant change to the coordinator to better handle Members that are in multiple Circles, especially where their data is different as seen by different Circles (e.g., a Member can share their location with some Circles but not with others.) But as long as you've showed me how to do that I'll go ahead and incorporate those changes. Thanks again!

As far as the other changes, it seems you caught a bug that got introduced when I had to abandon the idea of not updating when there is no data. So, I definitely need the check for `self._data` in the `entity_picture` method. (I'm not sure why that didn't manifest itself when I tested this. Hmm.) For the other properties/methods, it's not needed because they are not used/called when `self.available` is false.

> For the other properties/methods, it's not needed because they are not used/called when self.available is false.

If that is the case, we don't have to set `_data` to `None` either, meaning most of those guards can be scrapped, otherwise they should be guarded. Even if they aren't called when `self.available` is `False`, typing doesn't care. Behavior might change in the future as well. So adhering to possible outcomes from the possible return types is important.

issue_context.title: Life360 Entities go unavailable until reload of integration
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I’m running 2022.7.7, but I’ve had this issue with all 2022.7 builds.

Periodically if the internet flakes out, or perhaps an issue with life360 cloud, the entities for my people goes unavailable and they show as away in HA. If I ‘reload’ the integration they immediately recover and are ‘home’ again. Did not have this issue with the older-style integration on 2022.6 and prior.

I can reproduce the issue pretty consistently by killing internet access to HA and then restoring it. It requires a restart of the integration for the entities to update correctly again.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.7.x

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2022.6.x

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

life360

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

comments:
I still need to reproduce this behavior on a test system, but I believe what is happening is, after it is able to get good data from the server it still has the previous data, and since it is the same (in this particular case where the device probably isn't moving), it is not bothering to update the state. What it needs to do is to update the state, even if the data hasn't changed, IF the current state is unavailable.

I suspect if the device was moved, or the Life360 app was opened, the Life360 server would get new data (with a new `last_seen` timestamp), so the next time the HA integration updated (every 10 seconds), the entities would update properly.

I had the same issue when I upgraded to version 2022.7.7, but nothing I tried fixed the issue. I tried reloading the integration, updating the entity and even removing/re-adding the integration. Once I restored back to my previous version 2022.6.3, the integration started to work again.

> See also #75956

One thing to note - My person entities go 'away' when the life360 integration entities go unavailable. Sounds like based on this other thread that this isn't expected/intended behavior?

> My person entities go 'away' when the life360 integration entities go unavailable. Sounds like based on this other thread that this isn't expected/intended behavior?

Oh, interesting. No, that's not the expected behavior, at least not the way I read the person integration code. I'll have to give that a try.

I'm pretty convinced now that I should change the life360 integration so that it does _not_ use the `unavailable` state. Rather, when it can't get data from the server it should just keep the state it has. This is effectively the way it used to work. I'm going to look at other similar device tracker integrations to see what they do.

BTW, the bug reported in this incident becomes moot if I make that change, because it only happens _after_ the state goes to `unavailable`. If it never does, that can't happen.

> I had the same issue when I upgraded to version 2022.7.7, but nothing I tried fixed the issue. I tried reloading the integration, updating the entity and even removing/re-adding the integration. Once I restored back to my previous version 2022.6.3, the integration started to work again.

Are you sure you're not looking at the old, legacy, inoperable entities instead of the new ones? Have you read the breaking changes section of the 2022.7 release notes?

If you're sure it's the new entities that are stuck as unavailable, do you see any log messages that might shed some light? Have you tried enabling debug output for life360?

I was able to reproduce the behavior.

When I disconnected the network, the life360 `device_tracker` entities changed to `unavailable`, and a `person` entity based on one of them changed to `unknown`.

After reconnecting the network, the life360 entities eventually changed back to "normal" on their own (when the server had new different data for them.) And the `person` entity also changed back to normal.

FWIW, opening the Life360 app on my phone effectively forced new data and the corresponding HA entity changed back to normal almost immediately.

I'm still going to try to change the integration so that the entities never change to `unavailable` in the first place.
@pnbruckner Appreciate your work on this integration over the years; thanks for the work on the PR to correct this. Do you think a config option to disable the unavailable state would be acceptable?
@jerobins thank you. No, I'm positive that would not be accepted either. I'm going to close that PR and open a different one to fix the bug and not try to fight the issue of the unavailable state.
Was this issue solved? I still have it in 2022.8.3

> Was this issue solved? I still have it in 2022.8.3

The bug that prevented the entities from immediately returning to their normal state after server communications are re-established was fixed and released in 2022.8.1. If you think you still have _that_ issue, then please provide more details and I can re-open and investigate.

The behavior where the state of the entities becomes `unavailable` when server communications are disrupted is the behavior the core team wants and has required. So in their view this is not a bug or an issue. It is by design.

If you feel that is not the correct behavior, as others, including myself, do, then you'll need to convince the core team. I chose not to fight that fight beyond the attempt I already made. If you would like to pursue this, you'll need to open an Architecture Issue.

Please see the other issue and closed PR reference above for more details & background.
